answer: Each identity claims one flight of a spiral stair and locks an 80-credit bond. It files a key-signed log of step heights and tread wear from the canyon wall; an auditor re-measures it against the public stair table, and a mismatch over 2 percent, a reused log, or one key on two flights burns the bond. The first climb costs 36, the kth 36+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6030 and 1000 fakes pay 3,033,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-stair ring fails because rented logs carry another climber's wear and lack its vertex signature. An honest climber pays 36 once and recovers the bond after audit.
